- [USER] User expressed interest in illuminated manuscripts.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Notable artists and workshops that specialized in creating illuminated manuscripts include:
  - The Limbourg Brothers - a workshop of three Dutch brothers who created the famous Très Riches Heures du Duc de Berry manuscript.
  - The Book of Kells - a manuscript created by Irish monks in the 9th century.
  - The Tresor de Montsegur - a collection of manuscripts created by a group of Cathars in the 14th century.
  - The Winchester Bible - a manuscript illuminated by a team of artists in England in the 12th century.
  - The Hours of Catherine of Cleves - a manuscript created in the Netherlands in the 15th century.
- [USER] User recognized the Book of Kells and expressed surprise at the number of other notable works.
- [USER] User asked which illuminated manuscript the assistant thinks is the most impressive.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant stated it does not have opinions or preferences but noted that many consider The Book of Kells to be one of the most impressive illuminated manuscripts due to its intricate and colorful designs, particularly in the ornate initial letters. The assistant also mentioned that the Tres Riches Heures du Duc de Berry is considered a masterpiece due to its stunning depictions of the four seasons and richly detailed scenes of courtly life.
- [USER] User stated a fascination with illuminated manuscripts and inquired about exhibitions or museums where they can be seen in person.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant provided a list of museums and exhibitions where illuminated manuscripts can be seen in person, including:
  1. The British Library - located in London, with an extensive collection of illuminated manuscripts from various countries and periods.
  2. The Morgan Library and Museum - located in New York City, with a vast collection of medieval and Renaissance illuminated manuscripts.
  3. The Getty Center - located in Los Angeles, featuring illuminated manuscripts from various cultures and time periods.
  4. The Bibliothèque nationale de France - located in Paris, with an extensive collection including the Tres Riches Heures du Duc de Berry.
  5. The Vatican Library - located in Rome, with a collection that includes illuminated manuscripts from the Middle Ages.
  6. The Chester Beatty Library - located in Dublin, with an impressive collection of manuscripts, including illuminated manuscripts from the Middle East and Asia.
